coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Hearst Tower
record.summary: A 15-story (155 ft) student and postdoctoral-scholar housing tower in UCSF's Mission Bay housing complex, one of four buildings on Block 20 (with three mid-rise buildings that UCSF's housing page names the North, West and South buildings). The November 2002 UC Regents item anticipated full occupancy of the complex by October 2005; no source read states when it actually opened.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data and tax roll -- e.g. block/lot 8711507 (675 Mission Bay Blvd in DataSF's parcel data) alone is about 12.2 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.

facts.value: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) with Fisher Friedman Associates

UCSF student, postdoctoral scholar and family housing

One of four connected buildings (Hearst Tower, North Building, West Building, South Building) totaling 298,800 sq ft for more than 750 students, postdoctoral scholars and their families (Langan) around a shared at-grade courtyard

milestones.text: UC Regents' Grounds and Buildings and Finance committees approve, and vote to present to the Board, a $112,816,000 budget and external financing for the Mission Bay Block 20 Housing and Retail Project -- one 15-story tower (this building) and three mid-rise buildings (North, West and South/Student Housing), around a shared courtyard, 298,800 residential asf and 430 apartment units total -- with construction to begin June 2003 and full occupancy anticipated by October 2005

open_questions: Could not confirm whether all four housing buildings opened in exactly the same month, or whether some phased in slightly later than others.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, which could not be checked); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history. The same September 2008 Regents presentation (used for Byers Hall, Genentech Hall, Rock Hall and Rutter Center) includes one more photo on its "Architectural Context" slide labeled only "Housing," showing what looks like more than one building together; it wasn't used here because it can't be confidently attributed to this specific one.

As of 2026-09-21, the November 2002 Regents item's 430-unit, 298,800-asf, one-tower-plus-three-mid-rise description matches this record's own facts (431 apartments, 298,800 sq ft complex total) closely enough to identify Hearst Tower as the 15-story tower it describes, though the item covers the whole Block 20 project rather than naming Hearst Tower individually.

No cost figure specific to this tower alone (versus the whole four-building Block 20 project) was found as of 2026-09-23. The only figure found anywhere is the November 2002 Regents item's own $112,816,000 project budget, which the Regents item itself states as a whole-project total covering the tower and all three mid-rise buildings together -- no source breaks it down per building, so no cost is given for this building alone; the whole-project figure belongs with the site or phase, not with this one building.

Corrected 2026-09-29: this record earlier gave '431 apartments' and the address '1560 3rd St' for the tower alone. The Regents item gives 430 apartment-style units for the whole four-building project and Langan gives no unit count or street address; neither figure was found in a source that could be read, so both were removed.

Corrected 2026-09-29: no source read states when the building actually opened; the 2005 opening shown earlier rested only on a housing page that could not be checked and on Langan, which gives no date. The milestone now carries the October 2005 full occupancy anticipated by the November 2002 Regents item, marked expected. 'Student and faculty' was changed to 'student, postdoctoral scholar and family' housing because Langan and the Regents item say so and no source that could be read mentions faculty.

record.notes: Part of a single UCSF Mission Bay student housing complex (Hearst Tower plus North, West and South/Student Housing buildings; the building names come from UCSF's housing-office page, which could not be checked in September 2026) -- UC's Block 20 Housing and Retail Project: four buildings totaling 298,800 sq ft housing more than 750 UCSF students, postdoctoral scholars and their families around a shared courtyard (Langan). The November 2002 UC Regents item anticipated full occupancy by October 2005; no source read states the actual opening. Architect Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) with Fisher Friedman Associates (arcCA Digest: 'student apartment complex by SOM with Fisher-Friedman'). This building: Hearst Tower, 15 stories/155 ft (Langan). The Regents item gives 430 apartment-style units for all four buildings together; no source read gives a per-building unit count or a street address for the tower.
